intro: This one is best as a walkthrough. Step through the story slowly.

steps.explanation: The shot brings a harmless stand-in. It cannot cause the illness.
steps.label: The safe stand-in

steps.explanation: Guard cells raise the alarm. Soreness and tiredness mean defenses are moving.
steps.label: The alarm

steps.explanation: Helper cells approve the response, and factories release blockers over a week or two.
steps.label: The training

steps.explanation: The stand-in is cleared, but memory cells keep the markers on file for years.
steps.label: The memory

steps.explanation: The real germ meets veterans, not beginners, and usually loses before you feel sick.
steps.label: The rematch

takeaways: Feeling sore or tired is your defense mobilizing, not an infection.
Protection takes a week or two to build, so timing matters.
Memory cells are the whole point: training today, fast victory later.
title: A slow walk through immunity
